title: Bipartisan Robotics Panel Warns of Widening U.S. Deployment Gap With China
source_used: Unite.AI (page bylined to an AI-generated research agent)
key_facts: The National Security Commission on Robotics for Advanced Manufacturing, a bipartisan initiative of the Special Competitive Studies Project, released a 90-page Preliminary Report on 13 Oct 2026.

Its central finding is that the US leads in the 'brain' technologies (AI, vision, autonomy, software) but lacks the scale to deploy robots, produce robotic systems and make critical components domestically.
Citing International Federation of Robotics data, Chinese factories installed about 354,200 industrial robots in 2025 (59% of worldwide installations) against about 38,400 in the United States.
The report calls the problem a supply-demand paradox: manufacturers wait for cheaper, proven robots while robot makers cannot cut costs without deployment volume.
It also cites China's dominance of rare-earth magnet supply and security incidents involving Chinese-made robots, including a backdoor found in 2025 in a Unitree quadruped robot.
The commission calls the findings preliminary, notes its figures cover industrial robots and not humanoids, and schedules a Final Report with recommendations for March 2027.
Co-chairs are Senators Ted Budd (Republican, North Carolina) and Elissa Slotkin (Democrat, Michigan) and Ylli Bajraktari, president and CEO of the Special Competitive Studies Project.
quote_evidence: The report addresses physical AI, its term for artificial intelligence embodied in machines that sense and act in the real world, and argues that leadership will be determined by productive deployment and resilient production capacity rather than model capability alone.

According to International Federation of Robotics figures cited in the report, Chinese factories installed approximately 354,200 industrial robots in 2025, 59% of worldwide installations, compared with approximately 38,400 in the United States.
The commission frames the document as a diagnosis rather than a prescription; a Final Report with recommendations is scheduled for March 2027.
why_it_matters_hint: A bipartisan US commission says the country's robot software lead does not make up for being far behind China in deployment and production.
notes: Unite.AI's byline is an AI-generated research agent (Sophie Denar), reviewed by its editors; the claims are the commission's, as relayed by Unite.AI, and were not checked against the 90-page report itself.
